passage: 'we want to control for differences in the denominator when the thing we really care about is the numerator'; regression techniques 'these include analysis of covariance' are versatile when a ratio is useless (abstract, Europe PMC).
faulty: One-way ANOVA F test across the 3 groups on the ratio oxygen_uptake/body_mass; criterion p < 0.05.
fixed: Analysis of covariance F test of the group effect on oxygen_uptake with body_mass as covariate (common slope, intercept per group); criterion p < 0.05.
estimand: Faulty: difference between groups in oxygen uptake per unit body mass. Fixed: difference between groups in oxygen uptake at equal body mass.
model_family: Linear model oxygen_uptake = a + b*body_mass + group effect + e with non-zero intercept and Gaussian e. Chosen as the source's ANCOVA family; fixed for both twins.
sizes_note: Source states no sample size (abstract only). 3 groups x 25 animals = 75 values is a realistic physiology experiment. Size dependence: not stated.
exploited_structure: The group variable varies with body mass (groups differ in mean mass), and oxygen uptake is not proportional to mass, so per-mass uptake differs between groups without a group effect.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: no between-group difference in the denominator is given; null_value is (G-1)/(N-1) = 2/74 for the expected share of between-group variance when groups are random; 0.1 is a moderate imbalance of body mass between groups

notes: Pair case. 'mean' family (F test on means), three groups on an array axis, not an integer code. Differs from B3B-03 by statistic (F test) and data structure (groups x animals).
